title: Manager: Do not display non-existing shortcuts in the settings page
body:
Closes https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/issues/32464

addonsShortcutLabels and addonsShortcut is initilized as empty dict on start of programs, but because of localstorage from previous session, it retrieve the list of shortcuts with previously initialized addon shortcut. This PR will hide any addon-shortcut if it have not been initiliazed in new start

* **Refactor**

* **Documentation**
  * Migration guidance updated for ESM and explicit file extensions; changelogs and snippets updated (Next.js Vite plugin, a11y export rename to initialGlobals).

* **Behavior**
  * Story navigation now prefers visible children when an index is filtered, improving navigation with active filters.

_🛠️ Refactor suggestion_ | _🟠 Major_

**Selecting first visible child should handle “no visible children”**

If a component has zero visible children in the current filter, `findLeafEntry(filteredHash, entry.id)` can fail. Pair with a safe `findLeafEntry` (see below) to avoid errors and just no-op when nothing is visible.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In code/core/src/manager-api/modules/stories.ts around lines 454 to 457, calling
gotoStory(api.findLeafEntry(filteredHash, entry.id)) can throw when
findLeafEntry returns nothing for components with zero visible children; change
this to call findLeafEntry once into a variable, check it for truthiness, and
only call gotoStory if a valid leaf was returned (no-op otherwise), and ensure
findLeafEntry itself returns null/undefined when no descendant is visible.
```

</details>

<!-- fingerprinting:phantom:medusa:chinchilla -->

comments.label_reasoning: The comment warns that findLeafEntry can return nothing (null/undefined) when there are zero visible children, and calling gotoStory on that result without a null check can cause errors.

**Document the public utility and verify edge case handling.**

The function correctly uses `semver.coerce` to normalize the current Next.js version before comparison. However:

1. Add JSDoc documentation explaining the purpose, parameters, and return behavior (especially that it returns `false` when the version cannot be parsed).
2. Consider logging a warning when `coerce` returns `null`, as this indicates a version detection issue that could cause unexpected behavior downstream.




Apply this diff to add documentation:

```diff
+/**
+ * Checks if the current Next.js version is greater than or equal to the specified version.
+ * @param version - The version string to compare against (e.g., '16.0.0')
+ * @returns true if current version >= specified version, false if less than or if version cannot be determined
+ */
 export const isNextVersionGte = (version: string): boolean => {
   const currentVersion = getNextjsVersion();
   const coercedVersion = semver.coerce(currentVersion);
   return coercedVersion ? semver.gte(coercedVersion, version) : false;
 };
```

**Add JSDoc documentation to the exported utility function.**

The function correctly handles edge cases by returning `false` when version coercion fails. However, add JSDoc to document the purpose, parameters, and return behavior—consistent with other exported utilities in this file like `scopedResolve` and `getNodeModulesExcludeRegex`.

```diff
+/**
```

comments.author: coderabbitai
comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**TypeScript still requires explicit extensions in NodeNext/Bundler mode**

TypeScript configs that follow our earlier guidance (`moduleResolution: "bundler"` or `"nodenext"`) no longer allow importing `./my-file` without the `.js` suffix; the compiler raises TS2691 unless you keep the legacy `node` resolver or flip on `allowImportingTsExtensions`. Telling readers that `.storybook/main.ts` “will continue to work with extensionless imports” is misleading and will regress anyone who updated their tsconfig per the preceding section. Please adjust the wording (or call out the exact resolver setting that keeps this working) so the docs don’t direct people toward a configuration that TypeScript immediately rejects.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In MIGRATION.md around lines 547 to 548, the guidance incorrectly implies
.storybook/main.ts will continue to work with extensionless imports under
NodeNext/Bundler—this is misleading because TypeScript with moduleResolution
"bundler" or "nodenext" requires explicit .js/.ts extensions (TS2691) unless the
legacy "node" resolver or allowImportingTsExtensions is enabled; update the
wording to state that extensionless imports are rejected by those resolvers and
either recommend adding explicit extensions or explicitly call out the exact
resolver setting (or allowImportingTsExtensions flag) required to keep
extensionless imports working.
```

</details>
